newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil ex-president's son imitates father's suicide.
newsitem.headline: Brazil ex-president's son imitates father's suicide.

text.p: Maneco Vargas, the son of former Brazilian statesman Getulio Vargas, was found dead on Wednesday after apparently imitating the exact fashion of his father's suicide more than 42 years ago, officials said.

Vargas, 79, was found on his bed at his ranch in the region of Itaqui, 456 miles (730 km) west of Porto Alegre, with a bullet wound through his heart and a .38 calibre revolver lying next to him, a police officer said.
He left a note in the bedroom that read: "I don't intend to go down in history but simply to allow history to pass."
The note appeared to be an indirect reference to the suicide note left by his father, President Getulio Vargas, in which he said he was leaving the world of the living to go down in history.

Getulio Vargas, a two-time president and perhaps the most prominent Brazilian statesman of this century, was found dead in the Rio de Janeiro presidential palace on Aug. 24, 1954, after shooting himself through the heart.
Historians say Getulio Vargas committed suicide to prevent a military coup being plotted against him.
